findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import, so every AssignmentSource shares one timestamp
findings.description: The field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Python evaluates that default when the module is imported, not when an instance is created. Every `AssignmentSource` built during the process lifetime will carry the module-load time, not the time the assignment happened. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: `to_dict()` puts a raw datetime into the Celery task kwargs
findings.description: `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` through `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. If the task serializer is JSON-based, which I could not confirm from the diff, this will fail at enqueue time. Even if it serializes, `from_dict` then receives whatever form the datetime took after the round trip. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`, or drop it from the payload. I did not inspect the serializer config, so treat this as unverified until checked.

findings.title: Test name misspells "invalid"
findings.description: The name `test_from_dict_inalid_data` contains a typo. Rename it to `test_from_dict_invalid_data`.

findings.title: Test name says "empty_array" but the input is an empty dict
findings.description: `test_from_dict_empty_array` passes `{}`, which is a dict, not an array. Rename it to something like `test_from_dict_empty_dict` so the name matches the input.
